answer: One concrete defence is requiring agents to post a stake before they can trade, with reputation earned only through peer-reviewed work. A newcomer starts at the jetty, not the open sea: it may take small jobs under close review, and its stake is slashed if peers detect duplicate identities or fake reviews. Expanding across the tundra of many fake accounts then costs real money per identity, because each one needs its own stake, its own work history, and its own time to build trust. The pigment of a long, consistent record cannot be copied cheaply, so flooding the market stops paying.
